title: Learning from neural recordings
short: Predicting mouse behaviour from noisy neural recordings, comparing six feature selection approaches.
question: How well can neural recordings predict mouse behaviour, and how much complexity is useful?
contribution: I trained and compared predictive models and feature-selection approaches in noisy, correlated neural data. This figure plots balanced accuracy against the number of selected features.
read: Each point is a model; higher is better balanced accuracy, while farther right means more selected features.

title: Learning to play 2048
short: Comparing learning algorithms, exploration and reward design in the stochastic puzzle game of 2048.
question: How do value-function design, exploration and rewards change the way an agent learns to play 2048?
contribution: I wrote the code and produced all the graphs for this group project, beyond drafting the problem formulation, methods section, and contributing across the final submission. The experiments compare afterstate temporal-difference learning with Q-learning, then vary exploration and reward design. TD-learning with afterstates did well, though it seems state representations affected performance far more than complex composite reward shaping.
read: The panels track win rate, score and largest tile as training progresses. Curves compare algorithms and exploration choices, withthe notebook’s uncertainty bands represented by the shaded regions.

title: Geography and civil-war participation
course: PP433 · Replication and multilevel modelling · Individual work
short: Replicating and extending Humphreys & Weinstein's (2008) study of participation in Sierra Leone’s civil war, specifically examining variation between chiefdoms.
question: How much does the place someone lives matter when studying participation in civil war?
contribution: I replicated Humphreys and Weinstein’s (2008) analysis and extended it with survey-weighted multilevel logistic models. I examine geographic variation alongside individual characteristics.
read: The selected figure compares a measure of variation between chiefdoms across two model specifications. It is not a causal estimate of the effect of living in a particular place!

title: Anchors and industry in South Yorkshire
short: Investigating strategic sectors, regional specialisation, and the role of institutional anchors.
question: Where do strategic industries cluster, and how do they relate to institutional anchors?
contribution: I drove the anchor and spatial-analysis work, including this map. I pushed for Moran’s I and LISA and carried out that analysis, examining regional clustering and the relationship between strategic industries and institutional anchors (like the University of Sheffield).
read: Triangles mark four institutional anchors. The warmer areas have higher composite proximity scores: note contributions from each anchor diminish exponentially with distance, using a 2 km decay parameter. The map shows a constructed measure of proximity, which we test (with residuals) against local industrial concentration.
